title: Committee of Supply − Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: Private hire car driver licensing
sections.summary: Private hire car drivers must apply for a vocational licence with screening and training, addressing commuter safety and competency concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Private hire car drivers are now subject to regulatory requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: They, too, need to apply for a vocational licence which subjects them to screening and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This not only levelled the playing field with taxi drivers but, more importantly, addressed the safety and competency concerns of commuters.

sections.label: Taxi trips and private hire competition
sections.summary: Taxi trips stayed relatively stable from 2013 to 2016 while private hire cars tripled, prompting taxi operators to consider surge pricing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw had, in his reply to a Parliamentary Question on 20 February 2017, revealed that the total number of taxi trips remained relatively stable, with only a slight drop from 967,000 trips in 2013 to 954,000 trips in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: With private hire cars tripling in numbers since 2013, the statistics suggest that the "pie" for point-to-point transport has grown larger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The competition provided by private hire cars has now forced traditional taxi operators, who have been slow to change without competition, to consider revamping their pricing models in order to remain competitive and relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: There was news last week that several taxi operators, including ComfortDelgro, Trans Cab and Premier Taxi, were all considering implementing the surge pricing model used by private hire cars.

sections.label: Taxi drivers and transport disruption
sections.summary: Three events—private hire cars, diesel tax restructuring and driverless cars—may affect taxi drivers' livelihoods, and the Minister is asked for plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I do not advocate protectionist policies for our taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, in a reasonably short period of time, three events and their corresponding policies are likely to have repercussions on the livelihoods of taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: They are: firstly, the entry of private hire cars into the point-to-point transportation industry; secondly, the restructuring of the diesel tax; and thirdly, the push for automated, driverless cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: They are important for Singapore and will ensure that we maintain our competitive edge globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: And yet, all three together are likely to simultaneously cause specific groups of individuals, such as taxi drivers, frustration, worry and concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This is where policy-makers and public managers need to strike a fine balance between the two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share with us any of the Ministry's current and/or future plans to address the issues arising out of new technologies disrupting the transportation sector.

sections.label: MRT breakdowns and MKBF target
sections.summary: The Minister targets a Mean Kilometre before Failure of 400 kilometres, but recent breakdowns between Jurong East and Joo Koon inconvenienced Jurong residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Minister has set a very bold target of increasing the Mean Kilometre before Failure (MKBF) to 400 kilometres, a standard comparable to Hong Kong and Taiwan's sub-way, and this is laudable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the recent MRT breakdowns that concentrate between Jurong East and Joo Koon stations have greatly inconvenienced Jurong residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: There were at least three major breakdowns between these two stations in January alone and there are numerous incidents where the residents had to add tens of minutes of travelling time between the two stations.

sections.label: Reported train delays and breakdowns
sections.summary: Track circuit delays on the Clementi-Joo Koon stretch and at least 18 reported train breakdowns from May to December 2016 are cited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, half a dozen track circuit-related delays on the Clementi-Joo Koon stretch of the line have occurred in the past one and a half months, while a quick search on The Straits Times and TODAY from May to December 2016 brought up at least 18 times a train breakdown was reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, there are at least two breakdowns or more a month and these do not include the train faults and delays that were not reported.

sections.label: Productivity loss from train delays
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for the Ministry's assessment of recent breakdowns, citing man-hours and productivity lost to delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should also be greatly concerned with the loss of productivity to all our workers and our economy arising from the man-hours lost to all delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister what is the Ministry's assessment of the recent breakdowns?

sections.label: Public transport ridership and satisfaction
sections.summary: MRT, LRT and bus trips rose, satisfaction hit a nine-year high of 96.4% in 2016, and Hume residents face a 2.6 km unserved span.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the same year, MRT trips climbed 4.2% to 2.9 million, and LRT trips grew by almost 11%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Bus passenger trips were also up by 3.7% to 3.9 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Their efforts have paid off, as indicated by the latest annual Public Transport Customer Satisfaction Survey, where commuters' satisfaction in public transport scored 96.4% for 2016, hitting a nine-year high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Despite the presence of the Downtown Line's Hillview station, these Hume residents are caught in a long 2.6 km unserved span between Hillview and Beauty World MRT stations.

sections.label: Commuting to work or school
sections.summary: The 2015 General Household Survey found 59% of residents aged 15 and above took MRT and/or public bus to work or school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to the last General Household Survey in 2015, 59% of residents aged 15 years and above took the MRT and/or public bus to work or school.

sections.label: Connectivity to Bukit Gombak
sections.summary: The question asks whether LTA and MOT will help improve connectivity to MRT stations and access to the new Community Club in Bukit Gombak.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will LTA and MOT help to improve connectivity to MRT stations and access to the new Community Club in Bukit Gombak?

sections.label: Overcrowded buses in Nee Soon South
sections.summary: Bus services 860 and 811 from new BTOs to Khatib and Yishun MRT stations are over-packed, and Mandai Road and Sembawang residents lack a direct bus to Khatib.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The worst bus services in Nee Soon South are bus Nos 860 and 811 which pick up residents from new BTOs, like Acacia Breeze, Palm Breeze, Oleander Breeze, Angsana Breeze and Saraca Breeze, to Khatib MRT and Yishun MRT stations respectively.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is common to hear residents feedback that they must miss three or four buses before they can board as they are often over-packed − not so much of a "breeze" at all.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Besides that, my residents living in private estates in Mandai Road and Sembawang area have been telling me that Khatib is "so near and yet so far".

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is no direct bus to go to Khatib.

sections.label: Covered linkway at The Estuary
sections.summary: The Estuary previously declined an offer because LTA required a covered linkway from the nearest block to the back gate, and LTA has still not approved it.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, previously, it was offered to The Estuary but, at that time, they did not take it up because LTA had one caveat: they must build a covered linkway from the nearest block to their back gate, then LTA will continue from the back gate to the bus stop.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, this round, they agreed to do that but LTA's side has still not approved it.

sections.label: New public bus service standards
sections.summary: The BCM introduced new service standards that public bus operators are required to meet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The BCM introduced new service standards that the public bus operators are required to meet.

sections.label: First and last bus timing
sections.summary: The first and last buses leaving the terminal must reach their next stop within five minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In particular, the first and last buses leaving the terminal are required to reach their next stop no later than five minutes.

sections.label: Bus Service Enhancement Programme announced
sections.summary: In 2012, LTA announced the Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2012, LTA announced the Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP).

sections.label: Operators must use CFMS
sections.summary: The BCM requires all public bus operators to use LTA's Common Fleet Management System (CFMS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The BCM requires all public bus operators to use LTA's Common Fleet Management System (CFMS).

sections.label: Singapore Rail Academy training role
sections.summary: The new Singapore Rail Academy can train new entrants and upskill existing workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The new Singapore Rail Academy, recently launched, can play a vital role in training promising new entrants and also upskilling existing workers.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE quota contribution ceases
sections.summary: In this year's Budget, Minister Heng Swee Keat announced motorcycle COE quota contribution to open category COE quota would cease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, Minister Heng Swee Keat announced that the contribution of motorcycle COE quota to open category COE quota would cease, to address the problem of a decline in quota.

sections.label: Adding COEs to motorcycle categories
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOT would add COEs back to motorcycle categories to move towards the historical percentage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The recent effort to remove motorcycles from contributing to the Open Category COE is a good move, because it will mean more motorcycle COEs available than otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Despite that, however, the recent motorcycle COE auction price continued to edge up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, would MOT consider adding COEs back to the motorcycle categories, so that we move back towards the historical percentage that motorcycles used to represent in the entire vehicle population?

sections.label: Euro 6 diesel standards delay
sections.summary: MOT is asked whether it would delay Euro 6 diesel standards by one year from 1 January 2018 to let LGV vendors ready vehicles including manual transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, would MOT consider delaying the implementation of Euro 6 diesel standards by one year, from the current 1 January 2018, so as to give key LGV vendors time to ready the full range of vehicles, which includes more vehicles with manual transmission drive?

sections.label: Industry employment numbers
sections.summary: The industry collectively employs more than 300,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Collectively, the industry employs more than 300,000 workers.

sections.label: Infrastructure upgrading and technology projects
sections.summary: Infrastructure is being upgraded through concurrent projects and technology to raise productivity, including airports, terminals, rail lines, self check-in, robotics, driverless vehicles and drones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That is why we are continually upgrading our infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This year, we are working concurrently on multiple projects, including Changi Airport Terminals 4 and 5, the Pasir Panjang and Tuas Terminals, the KL-Singapore High Speed Rail, the JB−Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, the Downtown and Thomson-East Coast Lines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The scope for using technology to raise productivity is substantial − self check-in facilities at the airport, robotics for baggage handling, driverless cargo vehicles, automated cranes at our sea-ports, LTA using big data to optimise traffic flow, predictive maintenance for trains, and drones for all kinds of deliveries.

sections.label: Singapore Rail Academy launch
sections.summary: The Singapore Rail Academy was launched to nurture a Singapore Core with deep technical expertise, partnering e2i on a foundation programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Last month, I launched the Singapore Rail Academy, which aims to nurture a Singapore Core with deep technical expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: As a start, the Academy has partnered the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) to develop a foundation programme for both fresh graduates as well as mid-career upgraders.

sections.label: Rail network expansion
sections.summary: The rail network grows about one kilometre monthly, with the East-West Line extended four stations and Downtown Line 16 stations this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Our rail network is growing, on average, by one kilometre every month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This year, we will extend the East-West Line by four stations to Tuas West, and the Downtown Line by 16 stations to Singapore Expo.

sections.label: Households near rail stations
sections.summary: When all lines are completed, eight in 10 households will have a station within a 10-minute walk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: When all these lines are completed, eight in 10 households will have a station within a 10-minute walk.

sections.label: Downtown Line daily ridership
sections.summary: The entire Downtown Line should serve more than half a million commuters daily when in full operation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: When in full operation, the entire Downtown Line should serve a daily ridership of more than half a million commuters.

sections.label: Train-km target raised
sections.summary: Train-km improved to 192,000 in the second half, close to the 200,000 target, so the target is raised to 300,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It further improved to 192,000 train-km in the second half, close to my target of 200,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That is why I am raising the bar, to the next target of 300,000 train-km.

sections.label: Rail asset replacement and upgrading
sections.summary: Tenders will be called to upgrade the North-South and East-West Lines' power supply system and replace the first-generation MRT fleet with 66 new trains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The rail industry structure is now in a better shape to allow us to replace and upgrade ageing assets promptly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We will soon call tenders to upgrade the North-South and East-West Lines' power supply system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It has been a source of many problems in the last few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Now that we have taken over the assets, we are going to change this replacing of the power supply system, and also to replace all our first-generation MRT fleet with 66 new trains.

sections.label: Bukit Panjang LRT renewal
sections.summary: For the Bukit Panjang LRT, a tender is targeted this year for complete replacement of ageing components and a systems upgrade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: For the Bukit Panjang LRT, we have started the process for its renewal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We target to call a tender this year for a complete replacement of the ageing components and an upgrade of its systems.

sections.label: Bus Service Enhancement Programme
sections.summary: Under the Bus Service Enhancement Programme, 850 buses were injected and 70 new or amended routes introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Under the Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP), we have injected 850 buses and introduced 70 new or amended routes.

sections.label: Third bus package tender
sections.summary: Next month, the tender for the third bus package at Seletar will be awarded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Next month, we will be awarding the tender for the third bus package at Seletar.

sections.label: ARF increase for high-end motorcycles
sections.summary: The ARF increase applies only to high-end motorcycle models, so most motorcycle buyers will not pay higher ARF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This is the reason behind this move, because Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap had asked what was the rationale behind this move.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But we are increasing the ARF only for the high-end models.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The large majority of motorcycle buyers will not have to pay higher ARF.

sections.label: Concessions for commercial vehicle costs
sections.summary: Commercial vehicles have low ARF, motor taxes and road taxes, and can renew COEs repeatedly for five years to manage cash flow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That is why there are several concessions to help them manage costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: So, the ARF for commercial vehicles is low, motor taxes are low, road taxes are low for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: And, secondly, commercial vehicles can go for repeated five-year COE renewals to help businesses better manage their cash flow.

sections.label: Public bus service subsidies
sections.summary: Over the next five years, public bus services are expected to be subsidised by close to $4 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we expect to subsidise public bus services by close to $4 billion.

sections.label: Surge pricing and fare certainty
sections.summary: Taxi operators announced surge pricing, and many Singaporeans are concerned there is no longer fare certainty if taxis and private hire cars both adopt it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Recently, our taxi operators announced that they will be implementing surge pricing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The private hire car industry has set themselves up to fill the gaps in availability of the traditional taxi companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Now that taxi companies are moving in the same direction, many Singaporeans are concerned that there is no longer fare certainty if both the taxi firms and private car hires all adopt surge pricing.

sections.label: Idle taxis
sections.summary: Currently, more than 1,700 taxis are sitting idle.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, more than 1,700 taxis are sitting idle.

sections.label: Self-driving vehicle deployment timeline
sections.summary: Widespread deployment of self-driving vehicles is expected in 10 to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Widespread deployment of self-driving vehicles is expected in 10 to 15 years.

sections.label: Taxi Driver Vocational Licence holders
sections.summary: About 100,000 people hold a Taxi Driver Vocational Licence, and preparation of workers must start today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: But we need to start preparing our workers today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are about 100,000 people who possess a Taxi Driver Vocational Licence (TDVL).

sections.label: Wheelchair-accessible public buses
sections.summary: The Minister confirmed 92% of public buses are wheelchair-accessible, with a goal of 100% by 2020; SMRT buses fit two wheelchairs, some SBS Transit buses one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister previously confirmed that 92% of public buses today are wheelchair-accessible and the goal is to make this 100% by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the operators' websites, SMRT buses can accommodate two wheelchairs, while some SBS Transit buses can only accommodate one.

sections.label: More wheelchair space on buses
sections.summary: With an ageing population, a few wheelchair-bound persons may need the same bus, so the Government is asked to look into buses with more wheelchair space under the Bus Contracting Model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Besides their personal situation, they also rightly point out that as the general population ages, we can expect that a few wheelchair-bound persons may need to be on board the same bus at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Now with the Bus Contracting Model, where the Government owns all operating assets, I ask the Government to look into having buses with more wheelchair space.

sections.label: 2020 air pollutant reduction targets
sections.summary: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources was quoted stating Singapore was not on track to meet 2020 targets for reducing air pollutants.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recently, the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources was quoted in a newspaper article stating that Singapore was not on track to meet our 2020 targets for reducing air pollutants.

sections.label: Electric cars and public buses
sections.summary: The question asks if the Ministry has plans to promote private electric car ownership, and whether public buses would switch from diesel to electric.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Other than the sharing of charging points, does the Ministry have plans to promote private electric car ownership?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, since the Government's approach is to encourage public transport usage rather than private car usage, the key question when it comes to electric vehicles is whether our public buses would make the switch from diesel to electric.

sections.label: Footpath width reply by Khaw
sections.summary: Minister Khaw replied, and the speaker quotes, that most footpaths are at least 1.5 metres wide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Minister Khaw replied to say, and I quote, "most of our footpaths are at least 1.5 metres wide".

sections.label: Narrow Bedok North footpath
sections.summary: A footpath along Bedok North Avenue 4 near a bus stop and Block 95 is at least 1.2 metres wide in parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: One example is the footpath along Bedok North Avenue 4, specifically around the bus stop opposite St Anthony's Canossian Secondary School, right next to Block 95.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: It is 1.2 metres wide at least along certain parts of the path leading towards Bedok North Industrial Estate.

sections.label: Residents report accidents, LTA letter
sections.summary: Residents reported accidents and near misses, and a letter to LTA on 7 July 2016 has not been answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: According to the residents I spoke to, there have been accidents and near misses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I wrote a letter to LTA on 7 July 2016 but I have yet to hear from them on the action they may have decided to take or the reasons for not taking any action.

sections.label: Sixteen LTA enforcement officers
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question revealed there are currently only 16 LTA active mobility enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last month, I filed a Parliamentary Question and I learned that there are currently only 16 LTA active mobility enforcement officers.

sections.label: Volunteers versus dedicated enforcement officers
sections.summary: LTA should not rely only on its 600 volunteers, whose deterrent effect differs from dedicated enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: LTA should not just rely on its 600 volunteers as the deterrent effect and impact are not the same as having dedicated enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: We are on track to achieving a car-lite environment with a well-connected bus and train network, more sheltered walkways and the push for bicycles and PMDs.

sections.label: LTA Jurong Lake bicycle-sharing scheme
sections.summary: LTA's bicycle-sharing scheme will add 1,000 bicycles at fixed docking stations in Jurong Lake District by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In contrast, the bicycle-sharing scheme initiated by LTA will add 1,000 bicycles at fixed docking stations in the Jurong Lake District by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I understand that LTA is prepared to subsidise this bicycle-sharing scheme in Jurong Lake District.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: The companies bidding for this project will need to indicate the amount of subsidies they require.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: LTA's bicycle-sharing scheme, as compared to those provided by Ofo and Obike, appears to pale in comparison in terms of speed of implementation, the number of bicycles on offer and the ease of use.

sections.label: New trains and power supply sensors
sections.summary: All 66 new trains for the North-South East-West Lines and the new power supply system will have monitoring sensors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: All 66 new trains that the Minister mentioned for the North-South East-West Lines and our new power supply system will be equipped with monitoring sensors across all these.

sections.label: Predictive train maintenance approach
sections.summary: Data will enable a more proactive, predictive approach to train maintenance, replacing the current preventive maintenance model.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With such data, we will be able to improve the maintenance of our train system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will adopt a more proactive, predictive approach to maintenance, away from the current model of preventive maintenance.

sections.label: LTA analytics system data sources
sections.summary: LTA is building an analytics system fusing data from fare cards, wifi, CCTV and telco cellular data.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: LTA is building an analytics system which will fuse data from various sources, such as fare cards, wifi and CCTV systems, and also cellular data from the telcos.

sections.label: Private hire car trip share
sections.summary: PTC's recent survey suggests almost one in two point-to-point trips are now served by private hire cars.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: PTC's recent survey suggests that almost one in two point-to-point trips are now served by private hire cars.

sections.label: Fares vary with demand
sections.summary: Fares will likely vary with demand and supply, but commuters will know the exact fare before any journey begins.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Fares, indeed, will likely vary according to demand and supply, sometimes higher and sometimes lower during peak hours or off-peak periods.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: But importantly, before any journey begins, commuters will know exactly how much their fare would be.

sections.label: Private hire car licensing rules
sections.summary: From July 2017 private hire car drivers must obtain a vocational licence with training, tests and checks, while only taxis may serve street-hail.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From July 2017, private hire car drivers must obtain a vocational licence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To get the licence, they must undergo relevant training and pass requisite tests on road and passenger safety and be subject to background and medical checks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We intend to maintain some differentiation in privileges and regulations between taxi and private hire car services for now, given their different roles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For instance, we intend to continue to allow only taxis to serve the street-hail market.

sections.label: Taxi driver licence renewal fee
sections.summary: Active taxi drivers pay half the Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence renewal fee, $20, every three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Today, active taxi drivers pay only half of the Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence renewal fee, that is, $20, every three years when they renew their licence.

sections.label: Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme
sections.summary: Singapore is enhancing the Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme to incentivise lower emissions vehicles and will include pollutants like carbon monoxide and particulate matter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we are enhancing our Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme (CEVS) to incentivise a shift towards the purchase of lower emissions vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To more holistically account for the health and environmental impact of vehicular emissions, we will include other pollutants, such as carbon monoxide and particulate matter, into the criteria of the scheme.

sections.label: Hybrid and electric buses
sections.summary: LTA intends to expand the trial, calling tenders to procure 50 hybrid buses and 60 electric buses this year, with three bus services fully served by electric buses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: LTA intends to expand the trial and will be calling tenders to procure 50 hybrid buses and 60 electric buses this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will have three bus services which are fully served by electric buses.

sections.label: Open strollers on public buses
sections.summary: Starting from 2 April, families will be allowed to board public buses with open strollers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Starting from 2 April, we will allow families to board public buses with open strollers.

sections.label: Lifts at pedestrian overhead bridges
sections.summary: Lifts have been progressively installed at pedestrian overhead bridges, with 23 completed and 24 more by end-2018, though lifts cost about $4 million per pair and $40,000 yearly to maintain.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To improve pedestrian accessibility, we have been progressively installing lifts at pedestrian overhead bridges over the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We have completed 23 bridges so far and are working on another 24 to be completed by end-2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, lifts are not always the most optimal solution.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: They cost about $4 million in capital cost per pair of lifts and to maintain them takes about $40,000 a year.

sections.label: Programme expansion to 41 locations
sections.summary: The programme will be expanded to another 41 locations island-wide.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The programme will be expanded to another 41 locations island-wide.

sections.label: Widening narrow footpaths
sections.summary: Where possible, LTA will widen narrow footpaths with high pedestrian volumes from 1.5 metres or less to 1.8 metres or more.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Where possible, LTA will widen the narrow footpaths with high pedestrian volumes, from the current 1.5 metres or less, to 1.8 metres or more.

sections.label: LTA active mobility enforcement
sections.summary: LTA's Active Mobility Enforcement Officers conducted over 1,100 operations since May last year and advised over 1,300 riders for unsafe riding.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Since May last year, LTA's team of Active Mobility Enforcement Officers has conducted more than 1,100 operations and issued advisories to more than 1,300 riders for unsafe riding.

sections.label: Kra Canal and Malacca harbour
sections.summary: Thailand proposes a Kra Canal to bypass the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, and Malaysia proposes a new harbour along the Straits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thailand has a proposal to construct the Kra Canal, which would allow ships to by-pass the Straits of Malacca and Singapore altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Another proposal is by Malaysia to construct a new harbour along the Straits of Malacca that aims to overtake Singapore as the largest port in the region.

sections.label: Asia Pacific airport investment
sections.summary: A 2015 Centre for Asia Pacific Aviation study shows $226.8 billion will be invested in new and expanded Asia Pacific airports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: A 2015 study by the Centre for Asia Pacific Aviation shows that $226.8 billion will be invested in building new airports and expanding airport facilities in the Asia Pacific.

sections.label: China Malacca Gateway investment
sections.summary: Reports say China is investing S$14 billion in the Malacca Gateway Project, including a deep seaport island off Malacca ready by 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Recently, there have been reports that China is investing S$14 billion in the Malacca Gateway Project, which includes building a deep seaport on an island off Malacca which will be ready as soon as 2019.

sections.label: China financing Kra Canal
sections.summary: Reports say China is financing Thailand's Kra Canal so ships can go from the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea, bypassing the Straits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Similarly, there are also reports that China is financing the cost of Thailand's Kra Canal so that ships coming from the Indian Ocean can go straight to the South China Sea, bypassing the Straits of Malacca and Singapore.

sections.label: Oil spill response and accountability
sections.summary: Oil spills affected native diversity and fish farms; the passage asks about a roundtable for a comprehensive response plan and compensation for affected parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The recent oil spills severely affected native diversity and fish farms in the vicinity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MPA launched investigations into the cause of collision and various agencies conducted beach clean-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the SOP for clean-ups varies from agency to agency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider organising a roundtable to engage stakeholders and agencies, such as MPA, NEA, NParks and AVA, as well as other stakeholders and experts, to come up with a comprehensive oil spill response plan which can apply to future mishaps?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry hold responsible parties accountable for the impact and ensure that compensation is made to those affected, for example, the fish farms?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The aviation and maritime sectors contribute around 10% of our GDP and provide nearly 250,000 jobs.

sections.label: Tuas and Changi Terminal capacity
sections.summary: The new Tuas Terminal and Changi Terminal 5 will give capacity to handle twice today's passenger and container traffic volumes with room for growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the new Tuas Terminal and Changi Terminal 5, we will have the capacity to comfortably handle twice the volumes of passenger and container traffic today and still have room for growth.

sections.label: Air and Sea Transport ITMs
sections.summary: CAAS will launch the Air Transport ITM in April this year, and MPA will develop the Sea Transport ITM over the year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: CAAS will launch the Air Transport ITM in April this year, while MPA will develop the Sea Transport ITM over the course of the year.

sections.label: Container volume and error margin
sections.summary: Moving 30 million containers yearly makes even a small margin of error highly problematic, and Tuas will double that to 65 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And when 30 million containers are moved each year, even a small margin of error is highly problematic.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And imagine, at Tuas, we are going to get to double that volume − 65 million.

sections.label: T4 manpower savings from automation
sections.summary: At steady state, T4 is expected to realise up to 10% in manpower savings due to automation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Ang Hin Kee will be pleased to know that, at steady state, we expect T4 to realise up to 10% in manpower savings due to automation.

sections.label: Reduction in aircraft taxiing time
sections.summary: Since its implementation last year, one benefit has been a reduction of aircraft taxiing time by 90 seconds during peak hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since its implementation last year, one benefit has been the reduction of aircraft taxiing time by 90 seconds during peak hours.

sections.label: Singapore top international maritime centre
sections.summary: Singapore is ranked the world's top international maritime centre, with a diverse maritime services cluster of over 5,000 establishments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore is ranked as the world's top international maritime centre, with a diverse maritime services cluster comprising over 5,000 establishments.

sections.label: New shipping firms in Singapore
sections.summary: New companies like LH Shipping and West of England set up in Singapore last year, while K Line and Marubeni expanded.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: New companies, like LH Shipping from Switzerland and the West of England Protection & Indemnity Insurance Club, set up shop in Singapore last year, while those already here, such as K Line and Marubeni, expanded their operations.

sections.label: Singapore aviation and maritime certification
sections.summary: Singapore will be first in Asia with an IATA-certified pharmaceutical handling cluster, and SGX's Baltic Exchange acquisition aids maritime risk management.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singapore will be the first in Asia to build up a cluster of businesses certified by the International Air Transport Association in pharmaceutical handling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Similarly, the recent acquisition of the Baltic Exchange by SGX will allow Singapore to take active part in the fast-evolving landscape of maritime risk management.

sections.label: Shipulse installed on vessels
sections.summary: Shipulse has been installed on over 400 vessels and thousands more could use it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Shipulse has been installed on over 400 vessels and thousands more could use it.

sections.label: MPA Living Lab at port
sections.summary: MPA will set up the MPA Living Lab at the port by the end of this year to boost innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To give a further boost to innovation, MPA will set up the "MPA Living Lab" at our port by the end of this year.

sections.label: Air and sea transport jobs
sections.summary: About 13,000 new jobs are expected in the air and sea transport sectors by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: All in all, we expect some 13,000 new jobs in the air and sea transport sectors by 2025.

sections.label: SkillsFuture airport Earn and Learn
sections.summary: Two SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programmes for passenger service agents and ground operations specialists were introduced in October 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Two SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programmes for passenger service agents and ground operations specialists at the airport were introduced in October 2016.

sections.label: Sea transport skills training
sections.summary: Singaporeans will be trained in areas like data analytics and maritime technologies, benefiting about 5,000 locals annually, with a Sea Transport Skills Framework launching in April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This will enable Singaporeans to be trained in new and increasingly important areas, such as data analytics and new maritime technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We expect this to benefit some 5,000 locals annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Skills Framework for the Sea Transport sector, which was developed in consultation with the industry and unions, will be launched in April.

sections.label: ASEAN aviation agreements
sections.summary: All 10 ASEAN countries ratified the ASEAN open skies agreements last year, and ASEAN began negotiations on an EU-ASEAN Comprehensive Air Transport Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In aviation, last year, all 10 ASEAN countries ratified all the ASEAN open skies agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: ASEAN has also started negotiations on an EU-ASEAN Comprehensive Air Transport Agreement which would be the first bloc-to-bloc air services agreement in the world.

sections.label: Aircraft fuel savings trial
sections.summary: A 2016 operational trial showed each aircraft saved about 300 kilogrammes of fuel burn on average.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A 2016 operational trial showed that, on average, each aircraft saved about 300 kilogrammes of fuel burn.

sections.label: LNG bunkering pilot
sections.summary: MPA will soon pilot LNG bunkering operations in Singapore to promote adoption of cleaner marine fuels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To promote the adoption of cleaner marine fuels, MPA will soon pilot LNG bunkering operations in Singapore.

sections.label: Taxi phone booking standards
sections.summary: The Call Catering Quality of Standard yardstick may be removed from taxi operators' standards as the industry evolves, though some commuters still use phone bookings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: So, if that is already obsolete, will, therefore, the Call Catering Quality of Standard yardstick be removed from the taxi operators' standards?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We will look into all these as the industry evolves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: If the phone calling becomes completely displaced by apps, then maybe we will do away with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But there are still proportions of commuters that will be still using the phone bookings.

sections.label: New bus wheelchair stroller spaces
sections.summary: New standards for buying new buses require two spaces available either for wheelchairs or strollers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In the new standards that we have imposed on buying new buses, there will be two spaces available either for wheelchairs or strollers.

sections.label: Government bus subsidies
sections.summary: The Government is already subsidising $4 billion over the next four to five years on buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: As Minister Khaw mentioned just now, the Government is already subsidising $4 billion over the next four to five years on buses.

sections.label: Motorbike ARF and PARF
sections.summary: Extending the tiered ARF to motorbikes aims for more progressive taxation, and without PARF, deregistration incentives would be greater.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The reason for extending to motorbikes is not so much because of consistency but because we wanted this principle of being more progressive in our taxation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In other words, you get rid of your old vehicles, whether it is cars or motorbikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But because the bulk of the motorbikes, even with the tiered ARF, we will still be paying very low ARF, which is about 15% of Open Market Value (MOV).

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Without PARF, the incentives to deregister would be greater.

sections.label: China-UK freight train route
sections.summary: The China-UK freight train started in Yiwu and travelled through China, Kazakhstan, Russia, Belarus, Poland, Germany, Belgium, France and to London.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The China-UK freight train has started off in Yiwu and it has traversed across China, Kazakhstan, Russia, Belarus, Poland, Germany, Belgium, France and then to the UK, to London.

sections.label: China-UK freight link impact
sections.summary: The China-UK freight link does not appear to be a game-changer for the transhipment hub serving Asia-Europe traffic.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From that perspective, as a transhipment hub that serves quite a lot of the Asia-Europe traffic, for the moment it does not appear that the China-UK freight link is going to be a game-changer.

sections.label: Port workers and Tuas Terminal
sections.summary: About 8,000 to 9,000 local port workers will start to move from 2021 as Tuas Terminal gets its first berths operational.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Indeed, the union has been in discussion with us and has highlighted the concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are about 8,000 to 9,000 local port workers who, from the year 2021, will start to have to move as the Tuas Terminal gets its first few berths operational.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are very keen to make sure that the land transport options will be good ones.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are in discussions with other agencies and also with PSA which remains the biggest employer there.

sections.label: NGO input on oil dispersants
sections.summary: NGO inputs include non-toxic oil dispersants and prioritising containment, with protection for areas of greater bio-diversity value.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Some of the inputs that NGOs have given us include the use of non-toxic oil dispersants and also in terms of where we will prioritise the containment activities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What we have done is to say we will protect the areas that have got greater bio-diversity value.
